exact_quote: SEE ATTACHED (2 PAGES)   I AM COMPLETING THIS SUPPLEMENTAL REPORT AS OF 6.6.2018. THERE IS NO STAFF CURRENTLY EMPLOYED AT MARTIN GAS, INC. WHO WAS EMPLOYED AT THE TIME OF THE INCIDENT IN QUESTION. I CANNOT LOCATE A ""WORK FILE"" WHICH MIGHT CONTAIN THE INFORMATION THAT WAS CONTAINED WITHIN THIS PART H-NARRATIVE DESCRIPTION OF THE INCIDENT.
AN ELECTRIC UTILITY WAS INSTALLING A POWER POLE AT THE LOCATION OF THE INCIDENT AND AUGERED INTO A PLASTIC NATURAL GAS LINE CAUSING A RELEASE OF GAS.
THE GAS IGNITED, AND AN ELECTRIC UTILITY EMPLOYEE IN A CRANE BUCKET ABOVE THE DAMAGE WAS BURNED AND REQUIRED HOSPITALIZATION.

A SUPPLEMENTAL REPORT IS REQUIRED BECAUSE THE ELECTRIC UTILITY EMPLOYEE HOSPITALIZED AS A RESULT OF THIS INCIDENT PASSED AWAY DUE TO INJURIES SUSTAINED IN THE INCIDENT.  THE DEATH OCCURRED AFTER SUBMISSION OF THE INITIAL INCIDENT REPORT.
ORIGINAL REPORT FILED 11/03/10.    FINAL REPORT FILED 5/30/12 AT REQUEST OF PHMSA THROUGH COLORADO PUC.  NO NEW INFORMATION TO REPORT.
WHILE INSTALLING A POLY VALVE ASSENBLY ON A 2"" FLANGED STEEL PIPE STATIC ELECTRICITY IGNITED THE ESCAPING GAS.

THE CREW EXCAVATED THE PIPE AND DECIDED THAT THE CORRECTIONS WOULD BE MADE WITHOUT TURNING OFF THE GAS SOURCE TO THE PIPE BEING REPLACED.  AFTER CUTTING OUT APPROXIMATELY ELEVEN (11) FEET OF THE DAMAGED PIPE, THE CREW WAS ATTEMPTING TO INSTALL A PIECE OF 2"" PE 2406 PLASTIC USING TWO (2) DRESSER STYLE COUPLINGS.  WHILE ATTEMPTING TO MAKE THE CONNECTION, THE GAS WAS IGNITED BY AN UNKNOWN SOURCE WHICH RESULTED IN 1 DEATH AND 3 INJURIES TO GAS DEPARTMENT EMPLOYEES.

CONTRACTOR EMPLOYEE PURGED RESIDUAL NATURAL GAS WITH FORCED AIR OUT OF PIPE THAT WAS BEING ABANDONED INTO AN EXCAVATION WHERE TWO CONTRACTOR EMPLOYEES WERE WRAPPING PIPE.  THE NATURAL GAS/AIR MIXTURE WAS IGNITED BY OPEN FLAME ON A PROPANE TORCH THAT THE TWO CONTRACTOR EMPLOYEES WERE USING TO WRAP PIPE.

A WELDER FROM MICHELS WAS IN THE PROCESS OF WELDING AN END CAP ON THE OTHER END OF THE 8"" MAIN.  AFTER MAKING HIS INITIAL TACK, THE END OF THE PIPE THAT WAS TAPED AND SEALED WITH FOAM COMBUSTED OUTWARD BLOWING THE FOAM OUT AND BURNING THE MICHELS WELDER.
ABANDONED SECTION OF MAIN WAS NOT EVACUATED OF GAS.
MUNICIPALITY CUTTING ROAD WITH CONCRETE SAW DAMAGED 2 INCH PE GAS LINE.

A VERIZON SUBCONTRACTOR, FGC COMMUNICATION SERVICES (FGC), INSTALLING FIOS CABLE USED A PNEUMATIC TRENCHLESS TOOL, KNOWN AS A ""BULLET"" TO CROSS ZARRIELLO LANE IN WEST HAVERSTRAW, NEW YORK. THE ""BULLET"" PUNCTURED A 1991 VINTAGE TWO INCH PLASTIC GAS MAIN OPERATING AT  60 PSI.

APPROXIMATELY 45 MINUTES AFTER RECEIVING NOTIFICATION OF THE INCIDENT, 52 ZARRIELLO LANE EXPLODED. THERE WERE NO FATALITIES AND THE RESIDENTS WERE NOT HOME AT THE TIME OF THE INCIDENT. TWO LOCAL VOLUNTEER FIRE FIGHTERS WERE INJURED AS WERE TWO ORU GAS SERVICE TECHNICIANS.
THIRD PARTY INSTALLING FIBER OPTIC CABLE CUT 2"" PLASTIC MAIN.

BELL HOLES WERE DUG TO INSTALL A BYPASS AROUND THE DAMAGE.  EMPLOYEES INSTALLED TAPS ON EITHER SIDE OF THE DAMAGE.  AS EMPLOYEE BEGAN TO TAP OUT THE TAPPING TEE IN THE NORTH BELL HOLE, NATURAL GAS IGNITED AT APPROXIMATELY 17:15 HOURS ON APRIL 9, 2012.
THE ACTUAL SOURCE OF IGNITION IS UNDETERMINED.
EMT RESPONDED AND TRANSPORTED ONE (1) COMPANY EMPLOYEE TO HOSPITAL FOR BURN TREATMENT.

AFTER REMOVING THE SADDLE, THE CREWMEMBER ATTEMPTED TO ENLARGE THE HOLE USING A DRILL.  AN IGNITION AND FLASH OCCURRED.  IT WAS IMMEDIATELY EXTINGUISHED AND THE TAP HOLE RE-SEALED TO STOP THE FLOW.    TWO CONTRACTOR WORKERS WERE INJURED IN THE FLASH.  ONE WAS HELD AT THE HOSPITAL FOR FOUR DAYS FOR TREATMENT AND OBSERVATION.
USE OF IMPROPER TOOL DURING LIVE GAS OPERATION.
EXCAVATOR DRILLING TO INSTALL A UTILITY POLE DRILLED INTO AN ACCURATELY MARKED 4"" POLY MAIN WITH AN AUGER.  HOUSE EXPLODED BEFORE HAZARDOUS CONDITION WAS ELIMINATED.

HEARTLAND CONCLUDED THEY HAD EXPOSED THE ELECTRICAL LINE AND THE GAS LINE THAT USIC HAD MARKED. IN REALITY, HEARTLAND HAD EXPOSED TWO ELECTRICAL CONDUITS AND HAD NOT EXPOSED THE GAS MAIN.  HEARTLAND THEN DIRECTED THE DRILL TO A DEPTH ABOUT A FOOT BELOW THE CONDUITS AND STRUCK THE GAS MAIN.
ONE FATALITY AND MULTIPLE INJURIES RESULTED, INCLUDING MGE'S FIRST RESPONDER, AND EMPLOYEES OF HEARTLAND AND JJ'S RESTAURANT.
MGE'S FIRST RESPONDER, WAS TESTED FOR ALCOHOL AND DRUGS AFTER THE INCIDENT IN THE COURSE OF THE TREATMENT FOR HIS INJURIES AT ST. LUKE'S HOSPITAL, AND THAT THE RESULTS WERE NEGATIVE.
IT WAS REPORTED THAT THE DAMAGE OCCURED DURING EXCAVATION ACTIVITY BY THE CITY OF TULSA WATER AND SEWER DEPARTMENT.
THE SOURCE OF IGNITION WAS REPORTED TO BE A CUTTING TORCH BEING USED BY A MUNICIPAL EMPLOYEE.
ONE MUNICIPAL EMPLOYEE WAS TRANSPORTED TO THE HOSPITAL AND REMAINED OVERNIGHT FOR TREATMENT OF BURNS.

UPON ARRIVAL AT THE SCENE, THE COMPANY GAS DISTRIBUTION REPAIR CREW BEGAN TO HAND DIG TO LOCATE THE DAMAGE IN FRONT OF THE AFOREMENTIONED ADDRESS WHEN AN EXPLOSION OCCURRED AT 12:52 PM FOLLOWED BY AN IGNITION AND FIRE.
THERE WERE SEVEN PUBLIC SERVICE ELECTRIC & GAS EMPLOYEES AND THREE HENKELS & MCCOY EMPLOYEES THAT SUFFERED NON-LIFE THREATENING INJURIES THAT REQUIRED MEDICAL ATTENTION AND/OR HOSPITALIZATION.
WAS IN HER RESIDENCE
CONTRACTOR FOR THE OPERATOR WAS MAKING A TIE-IN FOR TWO 6"" POLY NATURAL GAS LINES.
LABORER TURNED AROUND TO CUT OFF GAS AT 2"" TAP.  NATURAL GAS IGNITED BEFORE THIS COULD HAPPEN.  LABORER CAUGHT ON FIRE AND SUSTAINED SECOND DEGREE BURNS TO ARMS AND FACE.

A CONTRACTOR PERFORMING ROAD RECONSTRUCTION AT THE INTERSECTION OF DORT HIGHWAY AND I-69 IN FLINT, MICHIGAN (GENESEE COUNTY) MADE CONTACT WITH AN 8""  PLASTIC GAS DISTRIBUTION MAIN, CAUSING A GOUGE IN ITS UPPER QUADRANT, AND RESULTING IN BLOWING GAS.

AT APPROXIMATELY 13:20 THE ESCAPING GAS IGNITED RESULTING IN A FIREBALL INJURING TWO MOTORISTS TRAVELING NORTHBOUND ON DORT HWY. ONE MOTORIST WAS TRANSPORTED BY EMS TO THE LOCAL HOSPITAL AND THE SECOND MOTORIST WAS TRANSPORTED TO THE LOCAL HOSPITAL BY PRIVATE VEHICLE. BOTH MOTORISTS SUSTAINED INJURIES THAT REQUIRED OVERNIGHT HOSPITALIZATION.
HOME OWNER HIRED A CONTRACTOR TO INSTALL SOME ""GEO LOCK EARTH ANCHORS"" TO STABILIZE THE BOWING/SHEERING OF FOUNDATION WALLS.
THIS WORK WAS COMPLETE IN SEPTEMBER OF 2014.  ONE OF THE ANCHORS EXTENDED IN EXCESS OF 10 FEET FROM THE HOUSE AND PUNCTURED THE MAIN IN THE ALLEY.
GAS MIGRATED VIA THE ANCHOR PATH TO THE FOUNDATION AND INTO THE HOUSE.  SOMETHING IGNITED THE GAS AND BOTH AN EXPLOSION AND FIRE ENSUED.

A CREAMER-SANZARI JOINT VENTURE CREW WORKING FOR PSE&G GAS DISTRIBUTION WAS IN THE PROCESS OF PREPARING TO PRESSURE TEST APPROXIMATELY 1200-FOOT OF 20-INCH STEEL.  ONE END OF THE MAIN WAS EXPOSED, AND A CREW WAS IN THE PROCESS OF EXCAVATING THE OTHER END WHEN A FAILURE OCCURRED.

TWO CREAMER-SANZARI JOINT VENTURE WORKERS WERE THROWN FROM THE EXCAVATION BY THE FORCE OF THE SUDDEN RELEASE OF THE PRESSURE, AND SUSTAINED SERIOUS INJURIES, WERE TAKEN TO JERSEY CITY MEDICAL CENTER-BARNABAS HEALTH WHERE THEY RECEIVED TREATMENT, AND WERE SUBSEQUENTLY RELEASED.
THE INCIDENT OCCURRED DURING PRESSURE TESTING OF PIPE.  AIR WAS INTRODUCED WHILE EXCAVATING THE END OF PIPE.

ONE EMPLOYEE FOR THE CONTRACT CREW WAS IN THE EXCAVATION WHEN THE PLASTIC MAIN WAS STRUCK BY ANOTHER EMPLOYEE OPERATING A BACKHOE WHERE  THE EMPLOYEE IN THE EXCAVATION WAS TAKEN TO THE HOSPITAL AS A PRECAUTION FOR CHEST PAINS.  THE COMPANY WAS ABLE TO LATER DETERMINE THAT THE EMPLOYEE WAS BEING HELD OVERNIGHT FOR OBSERVATION.

A THIRD PARTY EXCAVATOR WAS INSTALLING CONDUIT VIA DIRECTIONAL DRILLING.  A MAIN WAS STRUCK MULTIPLE TIMES DURING THE PULLBACK.  THE RELEASE OF GAS WAS SECURED ABOUT 2 HOURS PRIOR TO THE INCIDENT.  SUBSEQUENTLY, THE EXPLOSION OCCURRED.
AT THE TIME I ARRIVED HE STILL HAD GAS BLEEDING FROM THE SOUTH END OF THE LINE WHERE HE WAS WELDING ON SOMETHING AND GAS FROM THE NORTH END OF THE LINE WHICH WAS OPEN AND HAD BEEN SET ON FIRE.
A 2"" VALVE ON THE OUTLET SIDE TO SHAW HAD BEEN PREVIOUSLY TURNED OFF TRAPPING THE LINE PACK BETWEEN THE REGULATOR STATION AND SHAW WHICH IS ABOUT 350 FEET OF 4"" HDPE LINE.

EMPLOYEE 1 ATTEMPTED TO TIGHTEN THE PLUG INTO THE FITTING BUT THE PLUG BLEW FROM THE FITTING AND METAL SHAVINGS BLEW INTO EMPLOYEES ARM.  EMPLOYEE REQUIRED 3 NIGHTS OF  HOSPITALIZATION TO MONITOR INFECTION.

SUBSEQUENT INVESTIGATION DETERMINED THAT INADEQUATE JOB PLANNING, NOT FOLLOWING PROCEDURES, AND USING THE INCORRECT EQUIPMENT/TOOLS FOR THE JOB ALL CONTRIBUTED TO THE TAPPING AND STOPPING OPERATION FAILING AND THE SUBSEQUENT INJURY.

THE WELDER ATTEMPTED TO WELD THE PLUG SHUT AND IGNITED A SMALL AMOUNT OF GAS WHICH HE WAS UNAWARE WAS BYPASSING.  THE WELDER THEN ATTEMPTED TO ADJUST THE PLUG WITH A PIPE WRENCH INSTEAD OF EXTINGUISHING THE FLAME.  DURING THIS PROCESS, THE PLUG EVACUATED THE OPENING IN THE MAIN AND ALLOWED THE GAS FROM THE MAIN TO ESCAPE AND MAKE CONTACT WITH THE PREVIOUSLY IGNITED FLAME. WHILE HIS FR CLOTHING AND SAFETY GLASSES PROTECTED HIS UPPER TORSO AND EYES, THE PGW WELDER SUSTAINED BURNS TO HIS FACE AND NECK AND WAS TAKEN TO THE HOSPITAL BY THE PHILADELPHIA FIRE DEPARTMENT.

PERSONNEL MEMBERS 1 & 2 WERE CLEANING THE COATING ON THE PIPELINE TO PREPARE FOR A REPAIR CLAMP.  PERSONNEL MEMBER 3 WAS SUPERVISING THE REPAIR PROCESS.  PERSONNEL MEMBER 4 WAS USING A STEEL FILE TO PREPARE THE STEEL PIPELINE FOR CATHODIC ANODE INSTALLATION. THE INITIAL ATTEMPT TO TIGHTEN CLAMP WAS UNSUCCESSFUL TO SEAL THE LEAK.  TORQUE WRENCH WAS NOT USED IN THE INSTALLATION OF CLAMP. PERSONNEL MEMBER 3 THEN CHANGED POSITIONS WITH PERSONNEL MEMBER 1.  WHILE MOVING CLAMP IN AN ATTEMPT TO SEAL THE LEAK, IGNITION OF GAS OCCURRED.
UNKNOWN SOURCE CAUSED THE IGNITION OF THE GAS.

PERSONNEL MEMBER 2,3,4 WERE TRANSPORTED TO HOSPITAL FOR BURN INJURIES.  PERSONNEL MEMBERS 2 WAS TREATED AND RELEASED SHORTLY BEFORE MIDNIGHT ON 26 APRIL 18.  PERSONNEL MEMBERS 3 AND 4 SPENT SEVERAL DAYS IN BURN UNIT AT TULSA HOSPITAL.
A THIRD-PARTY EXCAVATOR HIRED BY THE TULSA HOUSING AUTHORITY (THA) HIT ONG'S 2"" MAIN.  ONG RESPONDED TO NOTIFICATION OF THE LINE HIT BY THE TULSA FIRE DEPARTMENT.
WHILE EXCAVATING TO SQUEEZE OFF THE LINE TO STOP THE FLOW OF GAS, ONG STRUCK AN UNMARKED, LIVE ELECTRICAL CONDUIT RESULTING IN AN IMMEDIATE IGNITION.

UPON ARRIVAL, THE WE ENERGIES  RESPONDER RECOGNIZED THE SIGNIFICANCE OF THE SITUATION BY THE LOCAL FIRST RESPONDER EVACUATIONS UNDERWAY. THE WE ENERGIES RESPONDER IMMEDIATELY CONTACTED GAS DISPATCH AND ASKED FOR ASSISTANCE.

AS A RESULT OF THE EXPLOSION, SEVEN LOCAL EMERGENCY RESPONDERS AND ONE WE ENERGIES EMPLOYEE WERE INJURED.  TWO FIRE FIGHTERS AND A WE ENERGIES EMPLOYEE WERE TRANSPORTED TO A NEARBY HOSPITAL.  WE ENERGIES WAS LATER INFORMED THAT ONE OF THE FIREFIGHTERS WHO WAS TRANSPORTED TO THE HOSPITAL HAD PASSED AWAY.  THE OTHER FIREFIGHTER TRANSPORTED TO THE HOSPITAL REQUIRED INPATIENT, OVERNIGHT HOSPITALIZATION AND THE WE ENERGIES EMPLOYEE TRANSPORTED TO THE HOSPITAL DID NOT REQUIRE INPATIENT, OVERNIGHT HOSPITALIZATION (UPDATED 1/2/19).
THE DAMAGED MAIN RELEASED GAS WHICH MIGRATED BELOW GRADE, INTO NEARBY BUILDINGS, AND  WAS IGNITED BY AN UNKNOWN SOURCE.
AN ADJACENT SEWER MAIN WAS ALSO DAMAGED.

GAS LEAKING FROM THE 2-INCH GAS MAIN ENTERED UNDERGROUND SEWER FACILITIES THROUGH THE DAMAGED PORTION OF THE SEWER MAIN AND THEN TRAVELED TO THE SEWER LATERAL FOR THE COFFEE SHOP LOCATED AT 23 E. DAME AVE., HOMERVILLE, GA.  AN INSPECTION OF THE COFFEE SHOP REVEALED AN IMPROPERLY PLACED P-TRAP, WHICH IS THE LIKELY PATH OF ENTRANCE OF THE NATURAL GAS INTO THE COFFEE SHOP.  THE GAS THAT ENTERED THE COFFEE SHOP THROUGH THE LATERAL WAS THEN IGNITED BY AN UNKNOWN IGNITION SOURCE.
THREE (3) INDIVIDUALS IN THE STRUCTURE WERE INJURED RESULTING IN HOSPITALIZATION.
THESE TWO WORKERS, PLUS A THIRD WORKER, WERE SAID TO HAVE BEEN DIGGING WITH SHOVELS AROUND A CAISSON CLOSE TO THE DAMAGED GAS MAIN.

THE OWNER AND FOREMAN ON SITE STATED THAT THERE WERE SEVERAL METAL SHAVINGS IN THEIR EXCAVATION AND MAYBE THEY HIT ONE OF THOSE OR THE CAISSON AND CAUSED A SPARK. THEY STATED THAT THEY WERE DIGGING AROUND THE CAISSON AND MOVING THE EARTH TOWARDS A TRENCHER THAT WAS REMOVING THE SPOIL. THE TRENCHER WAS SAID TO HAVE BEEN APPROXIMATELY 15 FEET SOUTH AND 5 FEET WEST OF THE DAMAGED GAS MAIN. OTHER WORKERS WHOM HAD SPOKEN WITH A PGL EMPLOYEE SAID THAT THE FIRE STARTED WHEN THEY STRUCK A TORCH THEY WERE GOING TO USE TO CUT THE CAISSON. IT IS CURRENTLY UNKNOWN IF TAYLOR EXCAVATING DAMAGED THE GAS MAIN WITH A SHOVEL, TORCH, OR THE BUCKET ON THE TRENCHER.

AN EMPLOYEE OF GOLDEN TRIANGLE CONSTRUCTION DUG INTO AN ACCURATELY MARKED 4-INCH MEDIUM PRESSURE PLASTIC GAS MAIN CAUSING DAMAGE TO THE PIPELINE.  UPON STRIKING THE PIPELINE AN UNKNOWN IGNITION SOURCE CAUSED THE ESCAPING GAS TO IGNITE.  THE GOLDEN TRIANGLE EMPLOYEE WAS BURNED BY THE FIRE AND WAS ADMITTED TO THE HOSPITAL FOR TREATMENT OF HIS INJURIES.

A THIRD PARTY EXCAVATOR DAMAGED THE PE MAIN DURING DIRECTIONAL BORING ACTIVITIES.  NO LOCATE REQUEST WAS RECEIVED FOR THE EXCAVATION.  THE LEAKING GAS APPEARS TO HAVE ENTERED AN ADJACENT RESIDENTIAL STRUCTURE AND EXPLODED, AND THIS CAUSED THE FATALITY, INJURIES, AND PROPERTY DAMAGE.
A CONSUMERS ENERGY DISTRIBUTION CREW DAMAGED A 2"" PLASTIC MEDIUM PRESSURE NATURAL GAS PIPELINE DURING A PIPELINE LOWERING PROJECT.

WHILE ATTEMPTING  TO EXPOSE THE PIPELINE DAMAGE, THE OPERATOR MADE CONTACT WITH THE ELECTRIC SERVICE LINE (LOCATED IN A JOINT TRENCH WITH APPROXIMATELY 19.5"" SEPARATION) CAUSING THE BLOWING GAS TO IGNITE. THE EMPLOYEE OPERATING THE EXCAVATION EQUIPMENT WAS INJURED AND THE EQUIPMENT AND BUILDING UNDER CONSTRUCTION WERE SIGNIFICANTLY DAMAGED BY FIRE.

WHILE A CONTRACTOR'S CREW WAS PERFORMING TAPPING OPERATIONS, A CREW MEMBER INADVERTENTLY BUMPED THE SLIDE VALVE OPEN AND NATURAL GAS WAS RELEASED.  THE CONTRACTOR HAS IDENTIFIED A GRINDER AT THE JOB SITE AS A PROBABLE SOURCE OF IGNITION.

THE CREW ENTERED THE EXCAVATION WITH INTENT TO TIGHTEN THE EXISTING CLAMPS TO REMEDY THE LEAK.  SAFETY PRECAUTIONS WERE IN PLACE INCLUDING ACTIVE MONITORING OF % GAS WITHIN THE BELL HOLE AND MANNED FIRE EXTINGUISHER.  AT NO TIME WAS A SIGNIFICANT RELEASE OF GAS HEARD OR RECORDED BY INSTRUMENT WHICH WOULD INDICATE A FLAMMABLE ENVIRONMENT.  HOWEVER, DURING THE REPAIR AT APPROX. 0935, NATURAL GAS IGNITED/FLASHED AND INJURED THREE CONSTRUCTION EMPLOYEES.
ALTHOUGH NO DIRECT SOURCE OF IGNITION HAS BEEN DETERMINED

WHILE THE TOR FITTING WAS BEING OBTAINED, THE CONTRACTOR'S FOREMAN DIRECTED HIS WELDER TO ATTEMPT TO IGNITE THE GAS IN THE NORTH TRENCH TO TEST FOR GAS.  THE SPARK TRAVELED DOWN THE PIPE TO THE SOUTH TRENCH AND IGNITED THE GAS THERE CAUSING AN INJURY TO THE EMPLOYEE.
WELDER FLASHED EXCAVATION HOLE WITH WELDING TORCH.
A CONTRACTOR (SEATTLE PUBLIC UTILITIES) HAD DUG INTO THE 2""PE PIPELINE WITH EXCAVATOR.

AT 11:07, WHILE GFR TECHNICIANS WERE IN THE PROCESS OF SQUEEZING THE PIPELINE TO STOP THE FLOW OF GAS, IGNITION OCCURRED. THREE FITTERS SUSTAINED BURNS AND WERE TAKEN TO HARBORVIEW MEDICAL CENTER AND ONE WAS ADMITTED TO THE HOSPITAL.

EMPLOYEES WERE REPAIRING A GAS LEAK BY ATTEMPTING TO INSTALL A BOLT ON LEAK CLAMP WITH A BATTERY POWERED IMPACT WRENCH WHEN GAS IGNITED. WHILE TIGHTENING THE BOLTS IGNITION OCCURRED BURNING TWO EMPLOYEES. BOTH EMPLOYEES WERE TRANSPORTED TO A HOSPITAL; ONE EMPLOYEE WAS TREATED AND RELEASED; THE OTHER EMPLOYEE WAS ADMITTED TO A BURN CENTER OVERNIGHT.

SPECIFICALLY THE BOLT ON REPAIR CLAMP WAS THE WRONG SIZE FOR THE PIPE BEING REPAIRED ; PROCEDURES PROHIBIT THE USE OF SPARK GENERATING EQUIPMENT IN A HAZARDOUS ATMOSPHERE; AND EMPLOYEES WERE NOT WEARING PROPER PPE CLOTHING.

WHILE CONTRACTOR (HALLEN) FOREMAN AND OPERATOR WERE WORKING IN THIS EXCAVATION WITH A LIVE GAS MAIN DRILLING A TAP HOLE, AN IGNITION OCCURRED RESULTING IN BOTH EMPLOYEES SUSTAINING SECOND DEGREE BURNS.

ROAD CONSTRUCTION CONTRACTOR, SEMA CONSTRUCTION, STRUCK A 2"" PE MAIN WHILE MIXING THE NEW ROAD BED. CONTRACTOR INITIALLY STRUCK THE LINE GOING EAST AND PROCEEDED TO WORK AS THEY WERE UNAWARE THE LINE WAS DAMAGED. CONTRACTOR THEN REVERSED COURSE, HEADING WEST, COMPLETELY SEVERING THE LINE. THE GAS THEN IGNITED AND EQUIPMENT CAUGHT ON FIRE RESULTING IN THIRD DEGREE BURNS TO THE WORKER. THE WORKER WAS TRANSPORTED TO THE HOSPITAL AND SUBSEQUENTLY ADMITTED.

OUR PIPELINE IN THIS SPECIFIC LOCATION IS POLY WITH NO TRACER WIRE. THE DISCUSSION BETWEEN THE WTG EMPLOYEE AND CONTRACTOR CONCLUDED: WTG WOULD BE ON SITE FIRST THING APRIL 21, 2020 TO FOLLOW WTG'S DAMAGE PREVENTION PROCEDURES FOR PIPELINES WITHOUT TRACER WIRE AND ASSIST IN LOCATING OUR PIPELINE. APPROXIMATELY TWO HOURS AFTER THIS ON-SITE MEETING BETWEEN THE WTG EMPLOYEE AND THE CONTRACTOR, WE RECEIVED NOTIFICATION FROM THE CONTRACTOR THAT HE HAD DUG INTO OUR PIPELINE.

EXCAVATOR (SUBCONTRACTOR) POT-HOLED ON MARKS TO VERIFY THAT GAS LINE WAS LOCATED WHERE MARKS INDICATED, BUT MIS-IDENTIFIED A DIFFERENT CABLE AS GAS PIPING.  BORING HEAD DAMAGED PIPE RESULTING IN SEPARATION OF 2 INCH PLASTIC MAIN.
CNP REPAIR CREWS WERE EXCAVATING IN REMOTE LOCATION TO ISOLATE SYSTEM AND REPLACE DAMAGED MAIN WHEN IGNITION OCCURRED.
THIRD-PARTY CONTRACTOR WAS INSTALLING TELECOMMUNICATIONS FIBER CABLE AND STRUCK A 2 INCH PE MAIN WITH A DIRECTIONAL DRILL.
NATURAL GAS MIGRATED INTO A STRUCTURE AT 50 COTTONWOOD PASS ROAD AND THE HOUSE EXPLODED, RESULTING IN THE DEATH OF AN OCCUPANT OF THE HOME.

THE DAMAGED GAS LINE RESULTED IN GAS MIGRATING INTO A SEVERED SEWER LINE WHICH WAS ALSO DAMAGED BY NEXT GENERATION MANAGEMENT INC. IN THE SAME EXCAVATION. IT APPEARS THE GAS MIGRATED FROM THE COUNTY SEWER SYSTEM THROUGH THE HOME'S SEWER SYSTEM AND UNEXPECTEDLY INTO THE HOME WHERE THE GAS IGNITED, RESULTING IN AN EXPLOSION.
WAS RUPTURED BY BORING WHILE A NON-AGLC CONTRACTOR WAS REPLACING UNDERGROUND ELECTRIC FACILITIES

AGLC BELIEVES THAT GAS FROM THE DAMAGED 1.25-INCH MAIN ACCUMULATED WITHIN ONE OF THE APARTMENTS NEAREST THE CUT LINE AND WAS THEN IGNITED BY AN UNKNOWN IGNITION SOURCE, CAUSING THE EXPLOSION AND ENSUING FIRE.
TWO AGLC EMPLOYEES, WHO WERE IN THE PROCESS OF EXPOSING FACILITIES TO IMPLEMENT FACILITY SHUTDOWN, SUFFERED BURN INJURIES FROM THE EXPLOSION AND FIRE.  NO OTHER INJURIES WERE REPORTED.

A CABLE CONTRACTOR, TEXAS BEST LLC, (WORKING UNDER EXPIRED LOCATE TICKETS), CONDUCTING DIRECTIONAL DRILLING OPERATIONS DAMAGED CENTERPOINT ENERGY'S 2"" INCH PLASTIC MAIN AT APPROXIMATELY 10:28AM ON MARCH 5, 2021.
ESCAPING GAS FROM THIRD-PARTY DAMAGE IGNITED AS CENTERPOINT ENERGY EMPLOYEES WERE WORKING IN A REMOTE BELL-HOLE TO STOP THE LEAK. SIX EMPLOYEES WERE INJURED, WITH THREE REQUIRING HOSPITALIZATION.

AFTER SUBSEQUENT INVESTIGATION IT WAS DETERMINED THAT GAS ESCAPING FROM THE DAMAGED TWO INCH PLASTIC MAIN MIGRATED TO THE REMOTE BELL-HOLE. WHILE EXPANDING THE BELL-HOLE CENTERPOINT CREW UTILIZING MECHANICAL EXCAVATION DAMAGED A (120 VOLT) STREET LIGHT CABLE WHICH RESULTED IN IGNITION OF MIGRATING GAS. THE RADIANT HEAT FROM THE BURNING GAS MELTED THE ALREADY EXPOSED SIX INCH PLASTIC MAIN THAT WAS IN THE BELL-HOLE.
A BGE CREW MEMBER RECEIVED SIGNIFICANT BURNS FROM A FIRE WHILE INSTALLING A WELD-OVER SLEEVE OVER A GAS MAIN COUPLING ON A DEAD-END BYPASS.

AFTER AN INTERNAL INVESTIGATION BY THE COMPANY, IT APPEARS THAT THE DEAD-END BYPASS SECTION WAS NOT BLOCKED/BRACED PRIOR TO CUTTING THE RESTRAINING STRAPS TO PERFORM THE WELD-OVER SLEEVE WELD OPERATION.   THE GAS PRESSURE FORCE CAUSED THE NON-RESTRAINING COUPLING TO GIVE WAY, WHICH RESULTED IN AN UNCONTROLLED RELEASE OF GAS WITH SUBSEQUENT IGNITION FROM THE WELDING EQUIPMENT.
DRAINAGE WORK WAS BEING PERFORMED BY WALK BEHIND TRENCHER ON THE RIGHT-AWAY OR UTILITY EASEMENT. CONTRACTOR HIT 2 INCH PE GAS LINE AND IT IGNITED. CONTRACTOR WAS BURNED AND SENT TO HOSPITAL.
EMERGENCY RESPONDERS INFORMED OPERATOR'S EMPLOYEES THAT ONE PERSON WAS INJURED AND HAD BEEN AIRLIFTED TO CABELL-HUNTINGTON HOSPITAL.

WHEN THE MAIN WAS EXPOSED, A SEWER CONNECTION FOR THE SECOND BUILDING WAS FOUND DIRECTLY OVER THE MAIN. CONCRETE HAD BEEN POURED OVER THE SEWER CONNECTION. OPERATOR'S EMPLOYEES DISCOVERED A GOUGE IN THE MAIN. A CLAMP WAS FOUND COVERING THE GOUGE. FASTENINGS ON THE CLAMP WERE CORRODED. THE DAMAGED SECTION OF MAIN AND THE CLAMP WERE RECOVERED AND ARE BEING PRESERVED.
BLUE PEAK TENTS, INC. PUT UP A TENT ON TUESDAY, 9/21/21.  THEY UTILIZED EXISTING HOLES IN THE PARKING LOT PAVEMENT, AND MADE A NEW HOLES IN THE PARKWAY FOR THE STAKES THAT HOLD DOWN THE TENT.

WHILE IN THE PROCESS OF REMOVING ONE OF THE STAKES, THERE WAS IGNITION OF NATURAL GAS. TWO EMPLOYEES FROM BLUE PEAK TENTS, INC. WERE INJURED. ONE EMPLOYEE WAS TAKEN TO THE HOSPITAL AND RELEASED THE FOLLOWING DAY, AND THE OTHER REFUSED MEDICAL ATTENTION.

BECKLEY WATER COMPANY WERE MAKING A WATER LEAK REPAIR AND CALLED IN AN EMERGENCY ONE-CALL TICKET. THEY DID NOT WAIT FOR UNDERGROUND UTILITIES TO BE LOCATED BEFORE DIGGING AND PUNCTURED MOUNTAINEER GAS COMPANY'S 2"" PLASTIC NATURAL GAS DISTRIBUTION PIPELINE OPERATING NEAR 30 PSIG.
MOUNTAINEER EMPLOYEES WERE DISPATCHED TO THE SCENE. WHILE INSTALLING A FULL CIRCLE BAND CLAMP, TWO OF THEM WERE OVERCOME WITH GAS AND REMOVED FROM THE LEAK AREA BY PERSONNEL ONSITE.
BOTH EMPLOYEES WERE GIVEN A MEDICAL ASSESSMENT AT THE HOSPITAL, ONE WAS ADMITTED TO INPATIENT HOSPITALIZATION FOR OBSERVATION, AND THE OTHER WAS RELEASED.

TECHNICIAN 3 THEN FITTED THE WRENCH INTO THE TOP OF THE COMPLETION PLUG. HE IS RIGHT HANDED SO HE PUT HIS LEFT HAND ON TOP OF THE WRENCH TO SECURE IT AND HIS RIGHT HAND ON THE HANDLE TO TURN IT. AS SOON AS HE STARTED TO TURN THE PLUG IT BLEW OUT THE TOP.
INJURED CITY EMPLOYEE WITH SHRAPNEL WOUNDS TO HIS LEFT FOREARM AND BICEP WITH SEVERE BLEEDING.

AT APPROXIMATELY 0300AM ON JUNE 8TH, THE FINAL COMPLETION PLUG HAD BEEN INSTALLED AND WAS BEING TIGHTENED WITH A WRENCH WHEN IT INADVERTENTLY BLEW OUT OF THE FITTING AND EXPOSED TWO COWORKERS TO A DIRECT STREAM OF GAS AT DISTRIBUTION PRESSURE. THIS RESULTED IN AN UNCONTROLLED RELEASE OF GAS WITHOUT IGNITION CAUSING INJURIES TO ONE COWORKER IN THE FORM OF METAL SHAVINGS LODGED IN THEIR FACE AND EYES. THE INJURED COWORKER WAS ALSO POTENTIALLY STRUCK IN THE HEAD WITH EITHER A TIGHTENING WRENCH AND OR THE COMPLETION PLUG WHEN THE COMPLETION PLUG BECAME DISLODGED.
THE DIRECT CAUSE FOR THIS INCIDENT IS INADEQUATE THREAD ENGAGEMENT DUE TO DEBRIS.

THE CREW HAD SUCCESSFULLY STOPPED THE FLOW OF GAS AND USED A 4-WHEEL CUTTER TO REMOVE THE PIPE.  ONCE THE PIPE WAS CUT, THE CREW BEGAN TO INSTALL THE WELD CAP, AT WHICH TIME THEY EXPERIENCED AN IGNITION OF GAS. THE IGNITION RESULTED IN THE INJURY OF ONE CENTERPOINT ENERGY EMPLOYEE.

GAS WAS BLEEDING PAST THE STOPPLE FITTING.  THE VALVE ON V1 VENT STACK WAS CLOSED. THIS RESULTED IN A PRESSURE BUILD-UP BETWEEN THE STOPPLE FITTING AND THE GRIPPER PLUG AND CAUSED THE GRIPPER PLUG TO BE EJECTED FROM THE OPEN-CUT END OF THE 12-INCH STEEL MAIN.  THE GRIPPER PLUG CAUSED A HAND INJURY WITH THE CONTRACTOR EMPLOYEE AND HE WAS ADMITTED TO THE HOSPITAL FOR TREATMENT.
SHAFER CONTRACTING CO., INC. DAMAGED AN UNMARKED 6"" PLASTIC CLASS 6 (50-55PSIG) GAS MAIN WITH A BACKHOE DURING ROAD RECONSTRUCTION WHILE WORKING UNDER GSOC TICKET #232891215.

NOTE, AT THE TIME OF THE DAMAGE THERE WAS NO EVIDENCE OF MINIMUM REPORTABLE CRITERIA FOR A MNOPS OR FEDOPS REPORT. IT WASN'T UNTIL A FIELD MEETING WITH MNDOT (JULIE) ON 10/24/23 THAT CENTERPOINT ENERGY'S DAMAGE PREVENTION COORDINATORS WERE MADE AWARE OF THE INJURY THAT OCCURRED ON THE DAY OF THE DAMAGE.
WHILE THE CONTRACTOR WAS PREPARING THE SUB-BASE FOR THE PROPOSED ROADWAY, THE CONTRACTOR CAME IN CONTACT WITH CNP FACILITY WITH ROAD RECLAIMER (ASPHALT GRINDER).
AFTER FURTHER REVIEW IT WAS DETERMINED THAT THIS 2"" POLYETHYLENE LINE WAS NOT AVAILABLE IN CNP MAPPING SYSTEM.

AN INVESTIGATION REVEALED A MISCOMMUNICATION AMONG THE CONTRACTOR EMPLOYEES REGARDING THE COMPLETION AND CONFIRMATION OF THE REMOVAL OF THE RESIDUAL GAS. THIS MISCOMMUNICATION OCCURRED BEFORE THE WELDER AND HIS HELPER ENTERED THE EXCAVATION TO PERFORM WELDING OPERATIONS. APPROXIMATELY FIVE MINUTES INTO THE WELDING PROCESS OF INSTALLING A WELD-OVER ON THE CONTROL FITTING USED TO ISOLATE THE MAIN, A FLASH FIRE IGNITED DUE TO THE REMAINING RESIDUAL GAS IN THE RETIRED SECTION OF THE MAIN.

BOTH CONTRACTOR EMPLOYEES WERE WEARING THEIR PERSONAL PROTECTIVE EQUIPMENT (PPE); HOWEVER, THE HELPER HAD REMOVED HIS GLOVES AND HELMET TO DRINK SOME WATER WHEN THE FLASH FIRE OCCURRED, RESULTING IN BURNS TO HIS FACE AND HANDS.
BOTH CONTRACTOR EMPLOYEES WERE TAKEN TO SEPARATE HOSPITALS. ONE CONTRACTOR EMPLOYEE WAS TREATED AND RELEASED, WHILE THE OTHER WAS ADMITTED TO THE HOSPITAL THE FOLLOWING MORNING.
